caption: What if you woke up with a dog's nose? You have about 6 million smell receptors. A dog has up to 300 million, and scientists estimate its sense of smell is 10,000 to 100,000 times sharper than ours. A dog could pick up one teaspoon of sugar in a million gallons of water, about one and a half Olympic pools. For its size, the smell-processing part of a dog's brain is about 40 times bigger than ours. About 12% of every sniff detours into a special smelling chamber, and dogs breathe out through the slits on the sides of their nose, so fresh smells keep flowing in. Each nostril sniffs on its own, which helps a dog tell which side a smell is coming from. Plot twist: in tests on 15 smells, humans were more sensitive than dogs to 5 of them, all found in fruits or flowers. What smell would YOU follow first? 👇
